# GEO report: trailhead **New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics. ## Code score: 46/100, At risk Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points). How it's calculated: low = 10.5 ÷ 23 × 100 = 46. High = (10.5 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 46. The code settles every applicable rule, so the score is a single number. The score is held down by three things: - The site renders only in the browser. - The `/guides` page is marked `noindex`. - Several basic signals are missing or too generic. No blocker applied, so the score isn't capped at 40. ## Live check - **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL. ## Do these first ### 1. Send real page content from the server (turn on server rendering) - **Why it matters:** Many crawlers read only the first HTML the server sends and don't run JavaScript. With rendering switched off, they get an empty shell for every page. - **Where:** `nuxt.config.ts:2` - **What the code says:** `ssr: false,` - **Size:** Small. Remove the line or set `ssr: true`. Alternatively, prerender the routes. - **Score after this:** 59/100 (10.5 + 3 = 13.5 ÷ 23). ### 2. Make `robots.txt` point to the sitemap with a full address - **Why it matters:** The `Sitemap:` line must be an absolute URL (including `https://` and the domain) so crawlers can find your page list. - **Where:** `public/robots.txt:4` - **What the code says:** `Sitemap: /sitemap.xml` - **Size:** Small. Use `https://trailhead.example/sitemap.xml`, the domain your sitemap already uses. - **Score after this:** 54/100 (12.5 ÷ 23). ### 3. Stop hiding `/guides` from search engines - **Why it matters:** `/guides` is in your sitemap and is your main content page, but a header tells search engines to skip it. That is a mixed signal. - **Where:** `server/middleware/headers.ts:3` - **What the code says:** `setResponseHeader(event, 'X-Robots-Tag', 'noindex');` - **Size:** Small. Remove this middleware, or limit it to pages that really should be private. - **Score after this:** 52/100 (12 ÷ 23). Doing all three gives 10.5 + 3 + 2 + 1.5 = 17 ÷ 23, which is 74/100. ## All results | Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | GEO-013 | robots.txt is readable and valid | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt` is plain text and well-formed | | GEO-009 | Search crawlers are allowed | Clear | Not run | `robots.txt:1-2` blocks only `/admin`. I assumed you want to be found. | | GEO-014 | Linked and sitemap pages are indexable | Problem | Not run | `/` is clear. `/guides` is noindex at `server/middleware/headers.ts:3` (1 of 2 routes clear). `/admin` is deliberately noindex and not counted. | | GEO-015 | One absolute canonical per page | Problem | Not run | No canonical anywhere (`app.vue:2`, `nuxt.config.ts:4-7`). Site-wide. | | GEO-003 | Content is in the server HTML | Problem | Not run | `nuxt.config.ts:2` `ssr: false`, with no prerendering. Both routes. | | GEO-004 | JSON-LD is valid | Not applicable | Not run | No JSON-LD in the project | | GEO-011 | Sitemap exists and is discoverable | Problem | Not run | `public/robots.txt:4` is a relative `Sitemap:` line. The sitemap file itself is valid. | | GEO-012 | Title, description, lang | Problem | Not run | `app.vue:2` `title: 'Trailhead'` and `nuxt.config.ts:6` give identical title and description on every route. `lang` is set (`nuxt.config.ts:5`). | | GEO-016 | Key pages reachable via real links | Problem | Not run | `pages/index.vue:8`, ``. Swapping to `` makes the page reachable by crawlers (this is the GEO-016 fix). - **Give each page its own title and description:** `pages/guides.vue:3-4`: `

Trail guides

` / `Routes graded from easy to strenuous.` This page shares the same "Trailhead" title as the home page. A `useHead` per page would tell visitors and machines which is which. - **Let crawlers see the `/admin` noindex, or drop it:** `public/robots.txt:2`: `Disallow: /admin`. `pages/admin.vue:2` adds `noindex`, but crawlers blocked by `robots.txt` never read it. Keep just one of the two, depending on your goal. - **The guides page is thin:** `pages/guides.vue:4`: `Routes graded from easy to strenuous.` It promises graded routes but lists none. Individual routes, each with its own page and address, would give readers and machines something to find. - **Add your site's address to the Nuxt config:** `nuxt.config.ts:1-9` has no site URL, while the sitemap uses `https://trailhead.example/` (`public/sitemap.xml:3`). A declared origin makes canonicals easy to generate. ## Can't tell from code - **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. To check, run `geopilot logs `, which tests real crawlers against their published addresses. - **Sitemap URLs:** the code can't show whether `https://trailhead.example/` and `/guides` actually answer 200. A live check would show that. ## Assumptions - You want search engines and AI search tools to find this site. - The `/admin` noindex is deliberate, so I didn't count it against you. - `trailhead.example` is a placeholder domain. Replace it with the real one when you fix the sitemap and canonicals. ## What to do next 1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written. 2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more. 3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL. Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
